title: Initial ridge-spur lake-road shore endpoint arrangement
scope: Qualitative upper-shore staging and seasonal-spur arrangement for the established lake road; usable for location, logistics, ecology, culture, and story development without establishing exact mapping, engineering, transport, infrastructure, staffing, shore use, ecological overlap, safety, guaranteed access, or new journey bands.
claims: The established lake road ends at one recurring upper-shore staging place.
The staging place is on relatively firm ground set back from the ordinarily shifting wet margin.
Several short seasonal spurs extend from the staging place toward nearby shore contacts.
Which shore contact is usable, and therefore which spur can serve as the final approach, can vary with seasonal and local conditions.
The staging place recurs while the final shore contact can change.
The staging place and any individual spur can flood, erode, ice over, attract wildlife, or become unusable; several spurs do not guarantee access at a particular time.
boundaries: This record is a forward refinement of WLD-LOCATION-001's qualitative lake-road relationship and WLD-LOCATION-002's open shore-endpoint boundary; it does not alter the settlement, managed apron, main road, lake, regional drainage, climate, habitat mosaic, migration relationships, or accepted journey anchors.

Upper-shore, relatively firm, set back, ordinarily shifting, several, short, seasonal, nearby, usable, staging place, and shore contact are qualitative author-facing relations; short is relative to the main lake road.

Recurring establishes a persistent selected location, not an exact mapped position, platform, terrace, clearing, building, fortification, storage site, processing site, workplace, staffed post, or operational guarantee.
Relative firmness and setback establish no surveyed flood line, dry ground, pavement, engineering, load rating, permanent stability, drainage, safety, maintenance, view, defence, or usability.

The staging place and any individual spur can flood, erode, ice over, attract wildlife, or become unusable; no particular flood, erosion episode, ice state, wildlife presence, closure, obstruction, damage, repair, bypass, reopening, abandonment, warning, encounter, or failed journey is established.
Several spurs do not guarantee that any usable shore contact exists at a particular time.

WLD-LOCATION-002 remains the sole authority for the broad 1–1½-hour downhill-unladen and 2–3-hour uphill-laden fair-weather whole-journey anchors; this record creates no staging-to-shore travel band and does not divide, extend, shorten, or recalculate either anchor, while exact time to the staging place, time along a spur, waiting, loading, and closure effects remain undefined.

WLD-ECOLOGY-004 continues to establish that secondary crown-herd paths overlap some roads and lake approaches; this record does not identify the staging place or any spur as one of those overlaps and guarantees no passage, closure, damage, warning, barrier, patrol, or response.

WLD-ECOLOGY-006 continues to establish broad lake productivity, seasonal migrants, shifting feeding grounds, predators, and human exploitation; this record places no spur through a nursery, migration route, fishing ground, predator concentration, harvest site, or other particular habitat, and establishes no organism, disturbance, population effect, or sustainable-use rule.
